children: U.S. Treasury yields moved in opposite directions on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 4%.
climbed to 4.65% from 4.60% just before the announcement. At the same time, the longer-end U.S. 30 Year Treasury yield
slipped to 5.31% from 5.33% just before the announcement.

The split flattened the curve. Front-end yields, which track near-term policy most closely, absorbed the first rate increase in more than three years and the official signal that another quarter-point hike is still penciled in for 2026.
Longer-dated yields eased as investors questioned whether growth and inflation will remain strong enough to support a higher terminal rate for long.

The Federal Open Market Committee’s move matched market expectations. Its Summary of Economic Projections showed policymakers anticipating one additional 25-basis-point increase later this year. That projection helped lift the 2-year note, while the modest decline in the 30-year suggested limited appetite to price a more aggressive path further out.
The reaction stayed orderly. Traders now look to incoming data to decide whether the extra tightening materializes or whether the long end continues to resist a higher-for-longer narrative.

title: Yields split after the Fed lifts rates to 4% with the shorter end of the curve rising
